But what we are selling here is the restaurant building itself. A single storey, substantially built rammed earth or pisé structure, surrounding a small open courtyard, extending to around xxx square metres and with a frontage and terrace directly to Ouarzazate’s Avenue Mohamed V.
An open terrace fronts Ouarzazate’s main thoroughfare. Double doors lead into the spacious restaurant, which still incorporates part of the original bar; a door with a keyhole arch leads to a private dining room, with a central passage leads to the central patio, kitchens, toilets and a service entrance.
Most of the surrounding, more recent buildings reach three storeys in height, meaning that as a development site alone there is considerable extra potential for the site. It’s worth considering the historic Bagatelle Restaurant in Marrakech, which was redeveloped from an old single storey building into a mixed development, with the restaurant occupying the ground floor of a building several stories in height.
